paper_title: From Zero to Hero Harnessing Transformers for Biomedical Named Entity   Recognition in Zero- and Few-shot Contexts
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: This pie chart depicts the distribution of named entity types recognized within a biomedical text corpus. The chart contains a total of 18 slices, each representing a different entity type. The largest slice, labeled “Chemical,” is colored red and accounts for approximately 32% of the whole. “Protein” is represented by a blue slice occupying 15%, while “DNA” is shown as a green slice at 6%. Smaller slices, generally appearing in clockwise order, include "Chemical Family" (5%), "Disease" (5%), "Cell Type" (5%), “Drug” (3%), “Frequency” (3%), “Cell Line” (3%), “Dosage” (3%), “Strength” (2%), “Form” (2%), “Gene Or Gene Product” (2%), “Disease Or Phenotypic Feature” (2%), “Specific Disease” (2%), “Reason” (2%), “Route” (1%), “Chemical Entity” (1%), “Sequence Variant” (1%), “Modifier” (1%), and "Organism Taxon" (1%). Percentage labels are included inside each slice. A legend is provided on the right side of the chart listing each entity type and corresponding color. No slices have been visually emphasized through offsetting or bolding.
